synth.title: Responsive reflow grammar (breakpoint behavior prior)
synth.principle_summary: A component reflows correctly across 375/768/1440 when its collapse behavior is chosen by CONTENT SHAPE, not by a single universal breakpoint ladder. Photo-grid and card-forward content (salon cards, galleries) holds its column count from desktop through tablet and drops to one column only at phone width; data-dense list-plus-panel content (filter sidebar, multi-field rows) collapses a full breakpoint earlier, going full-width and stacked already at tablet. Companion panels (a map, a detail pane) never shrink continuously alongside the main content; they are a binary toggle that is either present at full size or replaced by an open button. Filter/chip rows never wrap to a second line at any width; below the point where they would wrap, they become one horizontally-scrolling row instead. Compound controls (a search bar, a multi-field picker) either merge into one summary control (photo-grid discovery products) or stack each field as its own full-width row (transactional list products), and which mode a product uses is consistent for that product across every narrower breakpoint, not chosen per-breakpoint. None of this is yet expressed as a rule in Solen's own docs: LOCKFILE §7 states container widths and one grid recipe (`grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4`) as bare CONV device-class buckets with no stated collapse-order logic behind them, which is the exact gap this stream (G5) exists to fill.
synth.generative_prior:
Four concrete defaults, each with a threshold and 2-3 real-app examples, meant to make the FIRST mockup of a new responsive component right without guessing:

1. COLUMN-COLLAPSE THRESHOLD BY CONTENT SHAPE. Photo-grid/card content: hold column count from 1440 through 768, drop to 1 column only below 768 (i.e. only at the 375 phone tier). Evidence: Fresha salon search (fresha.com/search) is 2-col at both 1440 and 768, 1-col only at 375; Airbnb search results (airbnb.com/s/Zurich) shows the identical 2-col-hold-then-1-col-at-375 pattern. Data-dense list/panel content (a sidebar filter plus multi-field rows): collapse a full breakpoint earlier, going full-width stacked already at 768. Evidence: Booking.com's left filter sidebar and list-row cards both stack at 768, the same width where Fresha and Airbnb are still holding their desktop-like 2-column layout.

2. COMPANION PANEL = BINARY TOGGLE, NEVER A CONTINUOUS SHRINK. Below the width where a map/detail panel and the main content can no longer both hold a usable size (empirically ~768 in every case observed), replace the panel with a single open/close control rather than narrowing it. Evidence: Fresha's map panel becomes a small map-icon button at 768 that opens a full overlay; Airbnb's map becomes a floating "Show map" pill pinned bottom-center at 768; Turo exposes an explicit Grid/Map toggle in its top bar rather than trying to run both simultaneously below desktop width.

3. FILTER/CHIP ROWS SCROLL, NEVER WRAP. A filter or chip row stays one line at every breakpoint; below the width where it would wrap, it becomes horizontally scrollable instead. Evidence: Fresha's filter chip row at 375 has its rightmost "Price" chip visibly clipped at the viewport edge, direct proof of scroll-not-wrap; Airbnb's amenity chip row scrolls as one line at both 768 and 375.

4. COMPOUND-CONTROL COLLAPSE MODE IS PER-PRODUCT, NOT PER-BREAKPOINT. Discovery/photo-grid products merge a multi-field control into one summary pill (bold title line plus one comma-joined meta line) at every breakpoint below desktop. Transactional list products stack each field as its own full-width row instead. Evidence: Fresha's 3-field search bar (query, location, time) becomes one merged pill at both 768 and 375; Airbnb does the same, truncating text at 768 and going two-line at 375; Booking.com, by contrast, stacks destination and dates as separate full rows at 768, never merging. Solen's own locked `DateTimePicker` (one primitive: `dateLayout` strip for booking, calendar for search) already follows the merge model, so this evidence retroactively grounds a choice Solen made without a stated reflow rationale behind it.

Secondary, lower-confidence input: container queries (component-scoped reflow, not just page-level breakpoints) are CONV-supported by 2025-2026 industry sources at roughly 94% browser support as of December 2025, arguing that a shared component (e.g. a SalonCard reused in a narrow sidebar and a wide grid) should key its own layout off its container's width, not only the page's. This did not surface from the real-app scouting and is not yet backed by a Solen-specific example; treat as a framing to keep in mind for shared components, not a numbered rule to apply today.

TENSION FLAGGED, NOT REOPENED: LOCKFILE §7 (grid pattern set) currently sets the Solen search result grid to `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4`, adding a column at every step up. The two structural references this file claims to mirror (Fresha directly, Airbnb via LOCKFILE §1.5/§2.5 aesthetic lock) both instead HOLD 2 columns from tablet through desktop and only drop to 1 at phone, i.e. neither adds a third column at md. This is a genuine mismatch between the locked literal and the live behavior of the app it is meant to structurally mirror. Not proposing a change to the lock here; naming it so the owner can decide with the Taste Lab probe below rather than the mismatch sitting silent.
synth.proposed_addition:
### Responsive reflow grammar, a generative prior (gap G5, _design-system/research/PRINCIPLES_ROUND3/S05)

This is a PRIOR for building new responsive components, not a retrofit of an existing LOCKFILE literal. LOCKFILE §7.816-848 already states container widths and one grid recipe as bare CONV numbers with no collapse-order logic behind them (RATIONALE.md section 14, "Container widths and breakpoints" and "Grid pattern set" blocks); this section supplies the missing grammar so the next component is built once and reflows right the first time, instead of being retrofit after an owner catches a bad collapse.

PRIOR 1, column-collapse threshold by content shape: card/photo-grid content holds its column count from 1440 down through 768 and drops to 1 column only below 768; data-dense list-plus-panel content (a filter sidebar, multi-field rows) collapses a full breakpoint earlier and is already full-width-stacked at 768. Real-app evidence: Fresha and Airbnb search grids (2-col at both 1440 and 768, 1-col only at 375, T2 direct live-render capture) versus Booking.com (sidebar and list-rows both stack already at 768, T2 direct live-render capture, the explicit divergent case). Apply the "column" or "modular" Grid TYPE (LOCKFILE:840-848 classification) as card/photo-grid, and the "column" type used for dense row lists as the data-dense case, when deciding which threshold a new grid uses.

PRIOR 2, companion panel is a binary toggle: a map or detail panel running alongside main content does not shrink continuously as viewport narrows; below the width where both can no longer hold a usable size, it becomes a single open/close control (icon button or floating pill) instead. Evidence: Fresha map-to-icon-button and Airbnb map-to-floating-pill, both at 768 (T2 direct live-render); Turo's explicit Grid/Map top-bar toggle (T2, Mobbin capture).

PRIOR 3, filter/chip rows scroll, never wrap: a filter or chip row stays one line at every width; below the wrap point it becomes horizontally scrollable. Evidence: Fresha's chip row visibly clipping its rightmost chip at 375 (T2, direct proof via screenshot), Airbnb's amenity row scrolling at both 768 and 375 (T2).

PRIOR 4, compound-control collapse mode is chosen once per product, not per breakpoint: photo-grid discovery products merge a multi-field control into one summary pill at every narrower width; transactional list products stack each field as its own row instead. Evidence: Fresha and Airbnb both merge (T2, direct live-render); Booking.com stacks (T2, direct live-render, divergent case). Solen's locked `DateTimePicker` single-primitive design already matches the merge model; this is retroactive grounding, not a new requirement.

Secondary framing, not yet evidenced on a Solen surface: container queries (component-level, not just page-level, reflow) are CONV-supported at roughly 94% browser adoption as of December 2025 across independent 2025-2026 sources (LogRocket, DEV Community, UXPin). Worth keeping in mind for any shared component reused at genuinely different container widths (e.g. a card inside a narrow sidebar versus a wide grid); not asserted as a numbered rule here because no real-app or Solen example backs a specific threshold.

Explicitly rejected as an input: the 2025-2026 "bento grid" visual trend (mixed-size asymmetric cells) is CONV as a design trend but conflicts with Solen's 80/17 neutral-surface-plus-ink restraint and the no-decorative-artifacts rule; only its documented mobile collapse LOGIC (anchor element first, then supporting cells in priority order, single column below the threshold) is worth borrowing, never the dense asymmetric visual language itself. A separate unsourced claim that bento layouts increase dwell time or click-through is screened out as folklore (no named study, no publisher) and must not be cited.

TENSION, named not resolved: LOCKFILE's own search-result grid (`grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4`) adds a column at md where the two structural/aesthetic references it targets (Fresha, Airbnb) both instead hold 2 columns through tablet and drop straight to 1 at phone. Flagging for the Taste Lab probe below rather than changing the lock unilaterally.

TASTE LAB PROBE (per the repertory-grid method already logged in RATIONALE.md section, gap register D5): render Solen's own search-results grid at 768px in three real versions, current locked (`md:grid-cols-3`, three columns), Fresha/Airbnb-matched (hold 2 columns, drop to 1 only below 768), and a list-row alternative (single column, map behind a toggle button, matching Turo/Booking.com's denser mode). Show the owner all three at the SAME 768px width side by side, ask which reads right and why in their own words (not "pick A/B/C" but the triadic "which two are alike, how does the third differ" prompt), and use the answer to either retrofit LOCKFILE §7.816's grid recipe with a stated MECHANIC or explicitly confirm the current 2/3/4 ladder as an intentional Solen deviation from the Fresha/Airbnb reference, which it is not currently marked as.

synth.taste_lab_probe: Render Solen's search-results grid at 768px in three real versions built on the actual component: (A) current locked `md:grid-cols-3` three-column, (B) Fresha/Airbnb-matched, hold 2 columns through tablet and drop to 1 only below 768, (C) a denser list-row mode with the map behind an open/close toggle (Turo/Booking.com pattern). myths_caught: Container-query browser-support stat (~94% as of December 2025) is chronologically inconsistent with ground truth: caniuse.com's own live global usage-weighted figure (checked this pass) is 92.6% as of its current June-2026 snapshot. Browser support only grows over time, so a December-2025 figure should be LOWER than 92.6%, not higher at ~94%. The named secondary sources (LogRocket, DEV Community, UXPin) could not be independently re-verified this pass (WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-verification), so the specific magnitude is unconfirmed and directionally suspect. Softened in verified_addition to 'over 90%' with the caniuse contradiction noted rather than repeating the precise 94% figure.

The 'TENSION FLAGGED' section drops a qualifier that is present in the actual locked line. LOCKFILE:856 reads `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4 (2-col when map open)`, not a bare unconditional ladder. Both live Fresha and Airbnb renders this pass showed their grids WITH the map panel open, holding 2 columns, which is exactly what the Solen literal already specifies for the map-open case. The draft characterizes this as a flat, unexplained mismatch against the Fresha/Airbnb reference; it is at minimum an incomplete characterization, since the map-open branch may already match. The genuinely untested question is what the ladder does in the map-CLOSED state, which neither this stream's scouting nor this verification pass checked. Corrected in verified_addition and moved the open question to residual_risks with the accurate framing.

The retroactive-grounding claim for Solen's `DateTimePicker` overstates its own component doc. Reading `_design-system/components/DateTimePicker.md` directly: `dateLayout="calendar"` vs `"strip"` is a PER-PRODUCT-CONTEXT selection (search page always uses calendar, booking flow always uses strip), not a viewport-breakpoint-driven collapse of one field into a summary pill the way PRIOR 4 describes for Fresha/Airbnb/Booking.com. The component is real and the 'don't build a second date picker' lock is real, but citing it as evidence for the RESPONSIVE reflow prior conflates two different kinds of mode selection. Softened in verified_addition to describe it as a precedent for per-product (not per-breakpoint) compound-control mode selection, which is what it actually demonstrates.

The T3 'general web consensus on Airbnb's 6-5-4-3-2-1 column collapse' entry in real_world_evidence is directly contradicted by this stream's own T2 live-render finding (2-col hold through 768, drop straight to 1 at 375, no smooth multi-step descent), which I independently reconfirmed this pass. It is correctly kept out of the prose/proposed_addition and correctly tiered below the T2 direct observation, but sitting in the same evidence table as if it were corroborating rather than contradicted is misleading on a skim. Flagged in residual_risks for removal or an explicit 'contradicted by direct observation' note rather than deletion from verified_addition (owner call, not mine to silently cut).
verified.residual_risks: Owner-decision items: (1) The Taste Lab probe as drafted tests the LOCKFILE 2/3/4 ladder as a single undifferentiated case against Fresha/Airbnb's 2-hold-then-1 pattern. Since LOCKFILE:856 already carries a map-open/map-closed distinction the draft omitted, the probe should be split into two questions: does the map-OPEN state already match (likely yes, unverified), and does the map-CLOSED state need retrofitting (genuinely open). Recommend the owner get the corrected framing before the Taste Lab render is built, or the probe will burn a round testing a mismatch that may be partly resolved already. (2) The container-query stat should either be dropped to a qualitative claim ('most current browsers support container queries, exact percentage not independently confirmed this pass') or re-verified against the named LogRocket/DEV Community/UXPin sources directly once WebSearch budget resets; do not ship the precise ~94% figure into RATIONALE.md as-is. (3) Turo's evidence was upgraded this pass from Mobbin-only to a direct live render (I navigated turo.com/search myself and confirmed the Grid/Map toggle and the list-beside-persistent-map desktop layout), so that entry can be marked as independently confirmed, stronger than the draft's own T2 claim implied. (4) Fiverr/Faire/Unity Asset Store (T3, Mobbin-sourced) and the bento-grid mobile-collapse rule (CONV, trend-roundup-sourced) were not re-verified this pass; both are already appropriately low-tiered and low-stakes since neither is asserted as an operative numbered rule, so this is a note not a blocker. (5) The bento dwell-time/CTR MYTH catch in the original draft is correct and should stay cut, no action needed.
